claim: Free-space forecast for car parks, 15 min to 2 h ahead, tested on a year of Zurich open data
data_label: open data: City of Zurich car-park feed archive 2022 (CC0); weather: Open-Meteo
limit: One year, one city; guidance ties a live-count rule and only 56 % of full events are warned.
alt: Dark chart with two panels: forecast error in free spaces at 15, 60 and 120 minutes versus a weekly-naive baseline, and the share of cases where the recommended car park had space on arrival.
post:
You drive to a city-centre car park and the sign says FULL. How much of that could have been predicted an hour earlier?

I built an open-source forecaster for free spaces in multi-storey car parks, 15 minutes to 2 hours ahead. It uses recent readings, the same time last week, Zurich public holidays and weather, and gives an 80 % interval, a "full by" warning and a suggested nearby car park.

Test: a year of open data from 36 Zurich car parks, trained on January to August 2022, tested on the last 11 weeks:
- Error at 15 minutes: 2.9 free spaces, against 19.7 for a same-time-last-week baseline and 3.4 for "no change".
- 91 % of "full within 2 hours" warnings came true, but only 56 % of full events were warned in advance.
- When the intended car park was forecast full, the suggested alternative had space on arrival in 92 % of cases. Picking the nearby car park with the most free spaces right now scored the same.

Not verified: one year, one city, no live deployment, weather taken from observations, no driver behaviour in the loop.

Where would you want an honest "will it be full when I arrive" number first: city centre, hospital or event venue?

Code: https://github.com/VB-Builds/parking-occupancy-forecast
